## Data info

Where do the data come from? (To which population will results generalize?)

> The used grayscale photos are from CK+ database. The data includes 4 labeled emotions: anger, happiness, sadness, and surprise.
> The images are cropped to 48×48 pixels and converted to grayscale.
> The original source study recorded posed expressions from adults aged 18–50,
> mostly female (69%) and Euro-American (81%)
> ([Lucey et al., 2010](https://www.pitt.edu/~jeffcohn/CVPR2010_CK%2B2.pdf)).
> We expect the results to transfer to the similar posed expressions and photographic conditions.
> It is doubtful that the performance will generalize to images from uncontrolled conditions or other populations.

What are candidate machine learning methods? (models? features?)

> Classification trees and random forests, with PCA as an optional way to reduce the number of features.
> Raw pixels provide a simple baseline.
> Additional features should describe facial patterns.
> Other candidates (for later) include KNN, LDA, and SVM.

What is the Bayes' error bound? (Any guestimate from scientific literature or web resources?)

> Couldn't find a verified source for the Bayes error bound for this dataset.
> [Lucey et al. (2010)](https://www.pitt.edu/~jeffcohn/CVPR2010_CK%2B2.pdf) report classifier
> performance on seven emotions using a neutral expression as a reference,
> but it does not constitute a Bayes-error estimate for our dataset with 4 labels.
